Font is an application-owned input; no invented forced bitmap or universal Tahoma override. Source/system default and original application font behavior require per-path review.

design.root: src/lib-win32-style/appearance/win2000/{common,control,resources}; generic changes only at existing application owner with real current consumers
design.product: ntw2ks controls remains original API registration/ABI/style qualification assembly; delegates actual install/paint/remove to profile and existing public roots
design.instance: Win2000 control embeds style_instance and only needed common style_control_state/bindings; use lifecycle/install/instance/retire rather than another private subclass/list/lifetime manager
design.messages: Existing basic/list/edit/combo/native/scroll/notify/snapshot engines own protocol; profile supplies whole draw/qualification operations. No field-pointer view or copying Win3.x private control_style.
design.palette: Source semantic system-color slots, real Win2000 standard-scheme values from original imagery and accepted frame palette; no SetSysColors/registry/global theme modifications. Keep distinct bootstrap palette finding.
design.font_images: Borrow application HFONT/HICON/HBITMAP and existing parent color contract. Win2000 does not import Win3.x bitmap font/glyph tables. Any needed original resource requires named provenance and SHA before admission.
design.frame: Existing Win2000 frame/menu remains, adding nonclient scroll uses same public scroll roots; no second geometry/input/lifecycle implementation
design.creation: Keep original product hook/observation semantics and shared creation contracts; no new target/permission/propagation backend
design.S2_acceptance: Source-derived push/default/pressed/disabled/focus and supported image/text behavior, exact96DPI edge/palette samples from original image, actual Ntw2ksWindowAttach/Remove and --2k demo consumer, native keyboard/data/notifications/cleanup/reentry and Win16 regression; unavailable references are explicit, not hand-drawn guesses
